summary: Makoto Kitada is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who completed a doctoral course at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010) and Osaka University (attested 2026).

Makoto Nagai (1881–1970) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at Toyo University (~1928–1944), University of Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon University, and Kamakura Women's University.

Makoto Yoshimura (born 1969) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1995–2000) and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 2004.
Malati J. Shendge (born 1934) is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, Akira Hirakawa, and R. D. Vadekar.

Malay Porey is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned an M.A. from RKMVERI in 2014. He served as Assistant Professor at Durgapur Government College (2016), GGDC Ranibandh (2020–2025), and Acharya Brojendra Nath Seal College (2025).

Malcolm David Eckel (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Oxford and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held positions at Harvard (1980–1991) and Boston University (1990–2024).

Malcolm Huxter is a researcher in Buddhist studies and other fields. He completed a B.A. (Hons) at the University of New England (1985–1991) and earned a Master of Psychology at Charles Sturt University (1998–2002).

Malcolm Stuart Haughton Thompson (1885–1966) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Principal at Government College, Rajahmundry (1931–1932) and held a post at SOAS University of London.
Malcolm Voyce is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of London. He served as a professor at Macquarie University (attested 2009).

Mallica Kumbera Landrus is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. In 2026, she is attested as Keeper of Eastern Art and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the Ashmolean Museum, affiliated with the University of Oxford and Wolfson College.
Mamata Dash (born 1947) is a scholar in the field of Indology. She was educated at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami (1937–2024) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki, earning a doctorate in 1987, and served as professor at Kyoto University and Otani University.
Manabendu Banerjee (born 1939) is an Indologist who served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society. He also served as DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University (attested 2003).

Manabu Asano is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued PhD studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020) and served as a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Manasi Dilip Nadkarni is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She conducted doctoral research under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Manasicha Akepiyapornchai specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned a master's degree at Cornell University (2014–2022) and became an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin in 2022.

Mandan Mishra (1929–2001) worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal and Chief Editor at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (~1967–1989), Vice-Chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1993–1996), and held a post at the University of Rajasthan.

Manfred Mayrhofer (1926–2011) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz. He held professorships at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube (1928–2021) was an Indology and Tibetology scholar who studied under Friedrich Weller at the University of Leipzig (1949–1953). In 1991, he became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at the University of Leipzig.

Mangal Deva Shastri (1890–1976) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1937–1945).
